questions.question: The Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) was established in the year _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1948**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) was established in the year **1948**.
 
• IBM functions under the Ministry of Mines, Government of India.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in the conservation and scientific development of mineral resources.
 
• IBM is responsible for the regulation and development of the mining sector in India, including the inspection of mines and the promotion of sustainable mining practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functions of IBM:**

 
 
• IBM conducts mineral resource surveys and exploration programs.
 
• It provides technical consultancy services for the mining industry.
 
• IBM plays a significant role in the preparation and implementation of mining policies and regulations.
 
 
 
• **IBM's Role in Sustainable Mining:**
 
 
• IBM promotes sustainable mining practices to minimize environmental impact.
 
• It ensures the proper reclamation of mined areas for future use.
 
• IBM also oversees the implementation of safety standards in mines to protect workers.
 
 
 
• **IBM Publications:**
 
 
• IBM publishes various reports, statistics, and guidelines related to the mining sector.
 
• These publications are valuable resources for stakeholders in the mining industry.
 
 
 
• **Training and Development:**
 
 
• IBM conducts training programs for mining professionals to enhance their skills and knowledge.
 
• It collaborates with educational institutions for research and development in the field of mining.

questions.question: Nife layer of earth is situated in the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Core**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Nife layer of the Earth refers to its **inner core** and **outer core**, which are primarily composed of Nickel (Ni) and Iron (Fe).
 
• The Earth's core is divided into a solid inner core and a liquid outer core.
 
• The inner core has a radius of about 1,220 kilometers, while the outer core extends up to about 3,400 kilometers.
 
• The core is the hottest part of the Earth, with temperatures reaching up to 5,700 K (5,430 °C).
 
• The movement of the liquid outer core generates the Earth's magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earth's Layers:**

 
 
• The Earth is composed of three main layers: the crust, the mantle, and the core.
 
• The crust is the outermost layer, the mantle lies beneath the crust, and the core is the innermost layer.
 
• The mantle is made of silicate rocks that are rich in magnesium and iron.
 
 
 
• **Geological Terminology:**
 
 
• The lithosphere includes the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle.
 
• The asthenosphere is a semi-fluid layer upon which the lithosphere floats.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field:**
 
 
• The Earth's magnetic field is generated by the movement of molten iron and nickel in the outer core.
 
• This magnetic field protects the Earth from solar winds and cosmic radiation.
 
 
 
• **Plate Tectonics:**
 
 
• The movement of tectonic plates is driven by the heat from the Earth's core.
 
• This movement causes earthquakes, volcanic activity, and the formation of mountain ranges.

questions.question: Which of the following crops that spread to northern India in the early years of the 17th century was NOT mentioned in the Ain-i-Akbari in the lists of crops in northern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tobacco**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tobacco was introduced to India by the Portuguese in the late 16th century and became popular in the early 17th century.
 
• The Ain-i-Akbari, written by Abu'l-Fazl in the late 16th century, does not mention tobacco as it was not known in northern India at that time.
 
• The Ain-i-Akbari is a detailed document recording the administration of the Mughal emperor Akbar, including lists of crops grown in India during his reign.
 
• By the time tobacco became widespread in northern India, the Ain-i-Akbari had already been completed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tobacco Introduction:**

 
 
• Tobacco was brought to India by Portuguese traders in the 16th century.
 
• It quickly became popular in the Mughal court and among the general population.
 
 
 
• **Ain-i-Akbari:**
 
 
• The Ain-i-Akbari is part of the Akbarnama, a chronicle of Akbar's reign.
 
• It was written by Abu'l-Fazl, one of Akbar's court historians.
 
• The document provides a detailed account of the administration, culture, and economy of Akbar's empire.
 
 
 
• **Crops in Ain-i-Akbari:**
 
 
• The Ain-i-Akbari lists various crops such as wheat, barley, and pulses like arhar grown in northern India during Akbar's reign.
 
• It does not mention tobacco because it was not introduced or widespread at the time.
 
 
 
• **Portuguese Influence:**
 
 
• The Portuguese were responsible for introducing several new crops to India, including tobacco, maize, and cashew nuts.
 
• The introduction of these crops had a significant impact on Indian agriculture and cuisine.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Law and Justice Minister of independent India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BR Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **BR Ambedkar** was the first Law and Justice Minister of independent India.
 
• He served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee for the Indian Constitution.
 
• Ambedkar played a crucial role in framing the laws and policies for the newly independent nation.
 
• He was a key architect in establishing the legal and social framework of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law and Justice Ministry**:

 
 
• The Ministry is responsible for the administration of justice, legal reforms, and legal advice to the Government of India.
 
• It oversees the functioning of the legal and judicial system in the country.
 
 
 
• **Indian Constitution**:
 
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 January 1950.
 
• It is the supreme law of India and provides the framework for the political principles, procedures, and powers of government institutions.
 
 
 
• **Drafting Committee**:
 
 
• The Drafting Committee was formed on 29 August 1947 to draft the Constitution of India.
 
• BR Ambedkar was appointed as the Chairman of this committee.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms**:
 
 
• Ambedkar was a prominent social reformer and fought against social discrimination and the caste system.
 
• He played a significant role in uplifting the downtrodden and marginalized sections of society.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct according to the Census of India-2011?

(a) A person aged seven years or above, who can both read and write with understanding in any language, is treated as literate.

(b) A person who can only read but cannot write is not literate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (a) and (b) are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Census of India 2011 defines a literate person as someone aged seven years or above who can both read and write with understanding in any language.
 
• This definition explicitly excludes persons who can only read but cannot write.
 
• The Census aims to provide accurate data on literacy rates to help in policy formulation and educational planning.
 
• The Census of India is conducted every ten years to collect comprehensive demographic data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate:**

 
 
• The literacy rate is a key indicator of educational development in a country.
 
• According to the 2011 Census, the literacy rate in India was 74.04%.
 
• The male literacy rate was 82.14%, and the female literacy rate was 65.46%.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Literacy:**
 
 
• Literacy is crucial for the socio-economic development of a country.
 
• It empowers individuals with the knowledge to improve their quality of life.
 
• Higher literacy rates are associated with better health, economic productivity, and social stability.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Government of India has launched various schemes to improve literacy rates, such as Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.
 
• These schemes focus on providing free and compulsory education to children and promoting girls' education.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Despite progress, there are still challenges like regional disparities, gender gaps, and low quality of education in rural areas.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to address these issues and achieve higher literacy rates across the country.

questions.question: In May 2023, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been awarded the highest honours by the Pacific island nations of Papua New Guinea and ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In May 2023, Prime Minister Narendra Modi was awarded the highest honours by the Pacific island nations of Papua New Guinea and Fiji.
 
• During his visit, he received the "Companion of the Order of Fiji," which is Fiji's highest civilian honour.
 
• Similarly, he was conferred with the "Grand Companion of the Order of Logohu" in Papua New Guinea, the highest civilian honour there.
 
• These awards were in recognition of his efforts in strengthening India's relations with these nations and his leadership in global issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Order of Fiji**:

 
 
• The "Order of Fiji" is the highest honour awarded by the Fijian government.
 
• It recognizes exceptional service or achievement in any field by individuals.
 
• The award can be conferred upon both citizens of Fiji and foreign nationals.
 
 
 
• **Order of Logohu**:
 
 
• The "Order of Logohu" is Papua New Guinea's highest civilian honour.
 
• It is awarded for distinguished service to the nation in various fields such as public service, community service, and international relations.
 
• The Grand Companion of the Order of Logohu is the highest class within this order.
 
 
 
• **India and Fiji Relations**:
 
 
• India and Fiji share historical ties, with a large population of Indian origin residing in Fiji.
 
• Both countries collaborate in areas like trade, investment, and development cooperation.
 
• India provides scholarships to Fijian students and assists in capacity-building initiatives.
 
 
 
• **India and Papua New Guinea Relations**:
 
 
• India and Papua New Guinea have a growing bilateral relationship focused on economic cooperation and development.
 
• India has extended lines of credit and grants for various developmental projects in Papua New Guinea.
 
• Both countries cooperate in sectors like health, education, and infrastructure development.

questions.question: Which of the following articles mentions about the Appropriation Bills in the state legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 204**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 204** of the Indian Constitution deals with the Appropriation Bills in the State Legislature.
 
• An Appropriation Bill is introduced to provide for the appropriation out of the Consolidated Fund of the State for the services of a financial year.
 
• The Appropriation Bill is required to authorize the withdrawal of funds from the Consolidated Fund of the State to meet the expenditure during the financial year.
 
• Once the demands for grants have been voted by the legislative assembly, the Appropriation Bill is introduced in the legislative assembly for its passage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 216**: This article pertains to the constitution of High Courts in the states, specifying the number of judges in a High Court.
 
• **Article 209**: This article deals with the procedures for the introduction and passing of bills in the state legislature, other than money bills.
 
• **Article 213**: This article empowers the Governor of a state to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the state legislature.
 
• **Consolidated Fund of the State**: It is a fund where all revenues received by the state government, loans raised by the government, and all money received by the government in repayment of loans are credited.
 
• **Demand for Grants**: These are proposals for spending money by the government departments, which are put to vote in the legislative assembly.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__ __**__**Function of the President - France**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Function of President – France (Incorrect)
 
 
• India’s President is largely ceremonial (like UK), not executive.
 
• France has a semi-presidential system—its President holds real powers.
 
• Indian model is based on British parliamentary system, not French.
 
• Indian President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• Thus, matching “Function of President – France” is not accurate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rule of Law - Britain**

 
 
• Originated from A.V. Dicey, a British jurist.
 
• Emphasizes equality before law and supremacy of law.
 
• No one is above the law, including the government.
 
• Basis for Indian Constitution’s legal system and Article 14.
 
• Rule of Law is a foundational principle of British democracy
 
 
 
• **Procedure Established by Law - Japan**
 
 
• Japan follows the principle of "Procedure Established by Law" as mentioned in its Constitution.
 
• This principle implies that any law enacted by the legislature is valid if it follows the prescribed procedure, regardless of its fairness.
 
 
 
• Concurrent List – Australia 
 
 
• Borrowed from Australian Constitution.
 
• Both Union and States can legislate on subjects in this list.
 
• If there's a conflict, central law prevails (Article 254).
 
• India has 52 items (as of now) in the Concurrent List.
 
• Examples: education, forest, marriage, and adoption.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers**
 
 
• It is a doctrine that ensures the division of government responsibilities into distinct branches to prevent any one branch from exercising the core functions of another.
 
• The typical division includes the legislature, executive, and judiciary.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct about Ribosomes?

Statement A: Ribosomes have no membrane.

Statement B: Digestive hydrolytic enzymes are present in Ribosomes.

Statement C: These are called suicidal bags.

Statement D: Ribosomes play an important role in protein synthesis.

options.text: Only statements A, B and C

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statements A and D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ribosomes have no membrane**: Ribosomes are composed of RNA and proteins and do not have a surrounding membrane. They are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Ribosomes play an important role in protein synthesis**: They facilitate the linking of amino acids to form polypeptides, following the instructions encoded in messenger RNA (mRNA).
 
• Ribosomes can be found either floating freely in the cytoplasm or bound to the endoplasmic reticulum, forming rough ER.
 
• There are two main types of ribosomes: 70S (found in prokaryotes) and 80S (found in eukaryotes).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Digestive hydrolytic enzymes**: These enzymes are found in lysosomes, not ribosomes. Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes for breaking down cellular waste and macromolecules.
 
• **Suicidal bags**: Lysosomes are often referred to as "suicidal bags" because they can digest the cell's own components when they rupture.
 
• **Messenger RNA (mRNA)**: This type of RNA carries genetic information from DNA to the ribosome, where it is translated into a specific protein sequence.
 
• **Transfer RNA (tRNA)**: tRNA is responsible for bringing the correct amino acids to the ribosome during protein synthesis, matching the codons in the mRNA.
 
• **Ribosomal RNA (rRNA)**: This RNA forms the core of the ribosome's structure and catalyzes protein synthesis.

questions.question: 'Yakshagana', the famous folk dance, is associated with which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Yakshagana** is a traditional theatre form of Karnataka, primarily performed in the coastal districts.
 
• This art form combines **dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up, and stage techniques** with a unique style and form.
 
• The performances typically depict stories from Indian epics like the **Mahabharata** and **Ramayana**.
 
• Yakshagana is performed in the **Kannada and Tulu** languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Costumes and Makeup:** Yakshagana performers wear elaborate costumes and makeup, which are essential elements of the performance, giving it a vibrant and colorful appearance.
 
• **Musical Instruments:** The music in Yakshagana is provided by traditional instruments such as the chenda, maddale, harmonium, and chengila.
 
• **Types of Yakshagana:** There are two main styles of Yakshagana: Badagu Thittu (northern style) and Tenkutittu (southern style), which differ in presentation, costumes, and dance forms.
 
• **Historical Significance:** Yakshagana has a history dating back over 400 years and is believed to have evolved from pre-classical music and theatre art forms.
 
• **Modern Adaptations:** While traditionally performed overnight, modern Yakshagana performances have been adapted to fit shorter durations to cater to contemporary audiences.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) was launched by which Ministry of Government of India in the year 2016?

options.text: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Labour and Employment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment in August 2016.
 
• The scheme aims to incentivize employers for generating new employment and increasing social security benefits to the workers by providing wage subsidies.
 
• Under PMRPY, the Government pays the entire employer's contribution (12% or 8.33% as applicable) towards EPF and EPS for new employees for the first three years of their employment.
 
• This scheme targets establishments registered with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and encourages them to create new job opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)**

 
 
• EPFO is an organization under the Ministry of Labour and Employment responsible for regulating and managing provident funds in India.
 
• It provides social security benefits to employees in the form of provident fund, pension, and insurance schemes.
 
 
 
• **Employee Pension Scheme (EPS)**
 
 
• EPS is a pension scheme managed by the EPFO, aimed at providing pension benefits to employees in the organized sector after retirement.
 
• It is funded by diverting 8.33% of the employer's contribution from the employee's EPF account.
 
 
 
• **Skill India Mission**
 
 
• Launched in 2015, the Skill India Mission aims to train over 40 crore people in India in different skills by 2022.
 
• It includes initiatives like Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) and the National Skill Development Mission.
 
 
 
• **National Career Service (NCS)**
 
 
• NCS is a mission-mode project launched in 2015 to provide a variety of career-related services such as job matching, vocational guidance, career counseling, and information about skill development courses.
 
• It aims to bridge the gap between job seekers and employers using technology and provide employment services through digital platforms.

questions.question: The College of Fort William was established at ______ under British rule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The College of Fort William was established in **Calcutta** in 1800 by the British East India Company.
 
• This institution was founded by **Lord Wellesley**, the then Governor-General of India.
 
• The college aimed to train British civil servants in Indian languages and laws.
 
• It played a significant role in the **promotion of Oriental studies** and the translation of classical Indian texts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Wellesley**:

 
 
• Governor-General of India from 1798 to 1805.
 
• He implemented significant administrative reforms and expanded British territories in India.
 
 
 
• **Oriental Studies**:
 
 
• An academic field focusing on the languages, cultures, history, and societies of Asia.
 
• It includes the study of classical languages such as Sanskrit, Persian, and Arabic.
 
 
 
• **Translation of Classical Texts**:
 
 
• Key classical texts were translated into English, including the Mahabharata and the Ramayana.
 
• This helped in making Indian literature accessible to the Western world.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Education**:
 
 
• The College of Fort William set a precedent for higher education institutions in India.
 
• It laid the foundation for modern educational practices and the study of Indian languages and culture.

questions.question: Which of the following is a public sector industry in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)** is one of the largest public sector enterprises in India.
 
• SAIL is **owned and operated by the Government of India** and was established in 1954.
 
• It operates and manages five integrated steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur, Bokaro, and Burnpur.
 
• SAIL is responsible for the production of a wide range of steel products used in various industries including construction, engineering, and infrastructure.
 
• It is a **Maharatna company**, which allows it greater financial and operational autonomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs):**

 
 
• PSEs are companies in which the majority ownership is held by the government, either central or state.
 
• They play a critical role in the economic development of the country and are involved in various sectors including energy, mining, steel, heavy engineering, and more.
 
• Examples include Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), and Coal India Limited (CIL).
 
 
 
• **Maharatna Status:**
 
 
• Maharatna status is granted to PSEs that have recorded a net profit of over Rs 5,000 crore for three consecutive years, or a net worth of Rs 15,000 crore.
 
• This status provides greater investment and financial autonomy to the company, allowing them to make more independent decisions.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Steel Plant:**
 
 
• An integrated steel plant is a factory that combines various processes from raw material handling to steel production in one continuous process.
 
 
• **SAIL's Contribution:**
 
 
• SAIL contributes significantly to India's steel production and infrastructure development.
 
• It is also involved in various research and development activities to improve steel production technologies.

questions.question: What cellular structure is responsible for breaking down and recycling cellular components and molecules?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles found in animal cells.
 
• They contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down biomolecules, including proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids.
 
• They are often referred to as the "digestive system" of the cell due to their role in breaking down cellular waste and debris.
 
• Lysosomes are essential for cellular homeostasis, recycling cellular components through a process known as autophagy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Autophagy:**

 
 
• Autophagy is a cellular process that degrades and recycles cellular components.
 
• It helps maintain cellular health by removing damaged organelles and misfolded proteins.
 
• It plays a crucial role in cellular responses to stress and starvation.
 
 
 
• **Enzymatic Function:**
 
 
• Lysosomal enzymes are acidic hydrolases that function optimally at acidic pH.
 
• The acidic environment inside lysosomes is maintained by proton pumps in the lysosomal membrane.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomal Storage Diseases:**
 
 
• Lysosomal storage diseases are genetic disorders caused by the malfunction of lysosomal enzymes.
 
• Examples include Tay-Sachs disease, Gaucher's disease, and Pompe disease.
 
 
 
• **Role in Immune Response:**
 
 
• Lysosomes play a role in the immune response by digesting pathogens engulfed by phagocytic cells.
 
• They fuse with phagosomes to form phagolysosomes, where pathogens are degraded.

questions.question: In tennis, what is a 'love' score?

options.text: The score when the game is tied
The highest possible score in a game
The score when a player has zero points
The score when a player wins the first point in a game

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The score when a player has zero points**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Love** in tennis refers to a score of **zero points**.
 
• The term **"love"** is believed to come from the French word **"l'oeuf"**, meaning "egg," symbolizing zero.
 
• It is used at the start of the game and when a player has not yet scored any points.
 
• Tennis scoring progresses from love (zero) to 15, 30, 40, and game point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scoring System**: Tennis scoring is unique and progresses in a sequence: 0 (love), 15, 30, 40, and game point.
 
• **Deuce**: When both players have a score of 40, it's called a deuce. A player needs to win by two consecutive points to win the game from deuce.
 
• **Advantage**: After deuce, the player who wins the next point has the advantage. If they win the next point, they win the game; if they lose it, the score returns to deuce.
 
• **Set**: A set is won by the first player to win six games with at least a two-game lead.
 
• **Match**: Matches are typically played best of three or five sets, depending on the tournament rules.

questions.question: Which city hosted the XXII Commonwealth Games 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Birmingham**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The XXII Commonwealth Games 2022 were held in **Birmingham, England**.
 
• The event took place from **28 July to 8 August 2022**.
 
• Birmingham was chosen as the host city after Durban, South Africa was stripped of the Games in 2017 due to financial constraints.
 
• This was the third time England hosted the Commonwealth Games, previously hosting in London (1934) and Manchester (2002).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commonwealth Games**:

 
 
• A multi-sport event held every four years featuring athletes from the Commonwealth of Nations.
 
• The first Commonwealth Games were held in 1930 in Hamilton, Canada.
 
• It includes sports that are popular in Commonwealth countries, such as athletics, swimming, and netball.
 
 
 
• **Birmingham**:
 
 
• Located in the West Midlands region of England.
 
• Known for its industrial heritage and as a cultural hub with a rich history.
 
• Key venues for the Games included Alexander Stadium, Arena Birmingham, and the National Exhibition Centre.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact**:
 
 
• The Commonwealth Games are expected to bring significant economic benefits to the host city.
 
• Investments in infrastructure, tourism, and global exposure are key advantages.
 
 
 
• **Commonwealth Games Federation**:
 
 
• The organization responsible for the direction and control of the Commonwealth Games.
 
• Headquartered in London, England.
 
• Works to ensure the Games promote peace, equality, and inclusivity.

questions.question: Who is the recipient of Padma Vibhushan 2000 for reviving the Odissi Classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kelucharan Mohapatra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra** was a celebrated Indian classical dancer, guru, and exponent of the Odissi dance form.
 
• He is credited with **reviving and popularizing Odissi** as a major classical dance form.
 
• He received the **Padma Vibhushan in 2000** for his immense contribution to the art form.
 
• His **disciples include renowned dancers** such as Sanjukta Panigrahi, Sujata Mohapatra, and Kumkum Mohanty.
 
• Kelucharan Mohapatra also played a significant role in the **codification and systematization of Odissi dance techniques**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi Dance:**

 
 
• Odissi is one of the **classical dance forms of India**, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• It is known for its **intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculpturesque poses**.
 
• Odissi dance performances often narrate stories from **Hindu mythology, particularly those related to Lord Jagannath**.
 
• The dance form incorporates elements of both **folk and classical traditions**.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards:**
 
 
• The Padma Awards are one of the **highest civilian honors in India**, instituted in 1954.
 
• They are awarded in three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (for exceptional and distinguished service), **Padma Bhushan** (for distinguished service of high order), and **Padma Shri** (for distinguished service).
 
• Recipients are chosen based on their significant contributions in various fields such as art, literature, science, social work, and public affairs.
 
 
 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India:**
 
 
• India has several classical dance forms, each with its own unique style and tradition.
 
• Some of the prominent ones include **Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya**.
 
• These dance forms are recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first subcontinental empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mauryan Empire**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mauryan Empire was established by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE after overthrowing the Nanda Dynasty.
 
• It is considered the first pan-Indian empire, which unified most of the Indian subcontinent under a single political entity.
 
• The empire reached its zenith under Emperor Ashoka, who promoted the spread of Buddhism across Asia.
 
• The Mauryan Empire's capital was Pataliputra (modern-day Patna), which became a center of administration and culture.
 
• The Arthashastra, an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy, is attributed to Chanakya, the advisor to Chandragupta Maurya.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• Founded the Mauryan Empire with the help of his mentor and advisor Chanakya (Kautilya).
 
• His reign marked the beginning of a centralized and bureaucratic administration.
 
 
 
• **Emperor Ashoka:**
 
 
• Considered one of India's greatest emperors, he ruled from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• After the Kalinga War, he embraced Buddhism and promoted non-violence and Dharma (moral law).
 
• Ashoka's edicts, inscribed on pillars and rocks, spread his message of Buddhism and ethical governance.
 
 
 
• **Arthashastra:**
 
 
• An ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
 
• Attributed to Chanakya, it provides insights into governance, administration, and diplomacy during the Mauryan era.
 
 
 
• **Administration:**
 
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly centralized, with the emperor at the apex of a hierarchical bureaucracy.
 
• Provinces were governed by royal princes, and a network of spies ensured the smooth functioning of the empire.

questions.question: A molecule with the chemical formula C₂H₆ is a/an ______ molecule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ethane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ethane is a simple hydrocarbon with the chemical formula C₂H₆.
 
• It is a colorless, odorless gas at standard temperature and pressure.
 
• Ethane is the second simplest alkane, following methane, in the alkane series.
 
• It is primarily used as a petrochemical feedstock in the production of ethylene.
 
• Ethane is also present in natural gas and is separated during natural gas processing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkanes:**

 
 
• Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons, meaning they consist entirely of single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• They follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
 
• Alkanes are also known as paraffins and are found in natural gas and petroleum.
 
 
 
• **Ethylene:**
 
 
• Ethylene, with the chemical formula C₂H₄, is an important industrial organic chemical.
 
• It is produced from ethane through a process called steam cracking.
 
• Ethylene is used to make polyethylene, a common plastic.
 
 
 
• **Natural Gas Processing:**
 
 
• Natural gas processing involves separating various hydrocarbons and fluids from pure natural gas.
 
• Components like methane, ethane, propane, butanes, and pentanes are separated during this process.
 
 
 
• **Petrochemical Feedstock:**
 
 
• Petrochemical feedstocks are raw materials used in the production of chemicals derived from petroleum.
 
• Ethane is one of the primary feedstocks used to produce ethylene and other chemicals.

questions.question: What are the three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP of SHGs?

options.text: Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication
Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance
Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building
Social mobilisation, economic development, and education

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Social mobilisation** refers to the process of bringing together all societal sectors to raise awareness, demand, and participation for the empowerment and development of Self-Help Groups (SHGs).
 
• **Capital formation** involves the accumulation of assets and investments to generate income and enhance the financial stability of SHGs.
 
• **Capacity building** focuses on enhancing the skills, knowledge, and abilities of SHG members to improve their organizational and operational efficiency.
 
• These three components together aim to strengthen SHGs, enabling them to become self-reliant and sustainable in their economic activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**:

 
 
• SHGs are small, economically homogeneous affinity groups of rural poor, coming together to save and mutually contribute to a common fund.
 
• They provide members with support and resources to improve their living standards and economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance**:
 
 
• It is a financial service for low-income individuals or those who do not have access to typical banking services.
 
• Microfinance includes loans, savings, insurance, and fund transfers to help the underprivileged.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion**:
 
 
• It is the process of ensuring access to financial services and timely and adequate credit for vulnerable groups such as weaker sections and low-income groups at an affordable cost.
 
• Financial inclusion aims to connect people to the formal banking system to promote economic growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Livelihood Promotion**:
 
 
• It involves creating and enhancing opportunities for the poor to improve their income and employment prospects.
 
• Livelihood promotion includes training, skill development, and access to markets and financial services.

questions.question: The famous Qila-i-Kuhna (mosque of the old fort) was built by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sher Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque was built by **Sher Shah Suri**, the founder of the Suri Empire in India.
 
• It is located inside the Purana Qila (Old Fort) in Delhi, India.
 
• The mosque was constructed in **1541** during the short reign of Sher Shah Suri.
 
• It is an excellent example of early Mughal architecture, showcasing a blend of Indo-Islamic design elements.
 
• The mosque features a single domed prayer hall and is noted for its intricate stone carvings and decorative elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sher Shah Suri:**

 
 
• Sher Shah Suri, originally named Farid Khan, was a prominent ruler of the Suri Dynasty in North India.
 
• He is best known for his administrative reforms and the introduction of the "Rupiya," which was the precursor to the modern rupee.
 
• Sher Shah's reign is marked by significant infrastructure projects, including the construction of the Grand Trunk Road.
 
 
 
• **Purana Qila:**
 
 
• Purana Qila, also known as the Old Fort, is one of the oldest forts in Delhi, built by Sher Shah Suri and his predecessor Humayun.
 
• The fort is believed to be located at the site of Indraprastha, the legendary city of the Pandavas from the Mahabharata.
 
• It features massive walls, several gateways, and other historical monuments within its premises.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture:**
 
 
• Mughal architecture is a distinctive Indo-Islamic architectural style that developed in the Indian subcontinent during the Mughal Empire (1526–1857).
 
• It is characterized by large bulbous domes, slender minarets, massive halls, large vaulted gateways, and delicate ornamentation.
 
• Notable examples include the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and Humayun's Tomb.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Islamic Architecture:**
 
 
• Indo-Islamic architecture is a blend of Indian and Islamic architectural styles.
 
• It features elements such as arches, domes, minarets, and intricate geometric and floral patterns.
 
• This style emerged during the Delhi Sultanate and reached its zenith during the Mughal period.

questions.question: Which of the following states launched Mukhya Mantri Vriksh Sampada Yojana in March 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chhattisgarh launched the **Mukhya Mantri Vriksh Sampada Yojana** in March 2023.
 
• The scheme aims to boost the green cover and promote large-scale **tree plantation** in the state.
 
• It is part of the state's efforts to combat climate change and enhance **environmental sustainability**.
 
• The initiative is expected to help in the conservation of biodiversity and improve the **ecological balance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tree Plantation**:

 
 
• Tree plantation involves planting trees to restore and maintain forests and green areas.
 
• It plays a crucial role in mitigating climate change by absorbing carbon dioxide.
 
• Increases biodiversity by providing habitats for various species.
 
• Helps prevent soil erosion and maintains water cycles.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change Mitigation**:
 
 
• Efforts to reduce or prevent the emission of greenhouse gases.
 
• Includes renewable energy, energy efficiency, and reforestation.
 
• Essential for reducing the impact of climate change on the environment.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity Conservation**:
 
 
• The practice of protecting and managing biodiversity.
 
• Includes preserving species, their habitats, and ecosystems.
 
• Vital for maintaining ecological balance and supporting life on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Balance**:
 
 
• A state of dynamic equilibrium within ecosystems.
 
• Maintained through the interactions between living organisms and their environment.
 
• Essential for the sustainability of natural resources and overall environmental health.

questions.question: Which of the following award did Pandit Ravi Shankar win for four times?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Grammy Awards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pandit Ravi Shankar, the renowned sitar virtuoso, won the prestigious Grammy Awards four times during his illustrious career.
 
• He received his first Grammy Award in 1967 for "Best Chamber Music Performance" for the album "West Meets East" with violinist Yehudi Menuhin.
 
• Ravi Shankar won his second Grammy in 1972 for "The Concert for Bangladesh" in collaboration with George Harrison and others.
 
• He was honored with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2013, recognizing his contributions to the field of music.
 
• His fourth Grammy was awarded in 2002 for the album "Full Circle: Carnegie Hall 2000" in the category of "Best World Music Album".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Grammy Awards**:

 
 
• Established in 1959, the Grammy Awards are presented annually by the Recording Academy to recognize achievements in the music industry.
 
• The awards are considered one of the four major American entertainment awards, alongside the Oscars (film), Emmys (television), and Tonys (theater).
 
 
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar**:
 
 
• He was an Indian sitar player and composer, known for popularizing Indian classical music in the Western world.
 
• He collaborated with many international artists, including George Harrison of The Beatles, thus creating a significant impact on global music.
 
 
 
• **World Music**:
 
 
• World Music is a musical category encompassing many different styles of music from around the globe, which includes traditional music, non-Western music, and music where more than one cultural tradition intermingle.
 
 
 
• **Posthumous Awards**:
 
 
• A posthumous award is given after the recipient has passed away, acknowledging their contributions or achievements.
